chapter: Minton's, Louis Armstrong and the South
title: Max Roach and Art Blakey at Minton's and Monroe's Uptown House
summary: Max Roach, 15 when Clarke played Kelly's Stables, learned from him at Minton's; after hours they all went to Monroe's Uptown House to talk drumming.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Let's just talk about the drummers a second, because it's very interesting, because I mean this must have been their big exciting time too, when the world opened up and they heard something that knocked them out.
I mean what about -- well, just talk to me. I mean what about Max, Max Roach?
Oh, Max came after. We -- well, Max was 15 when we were at Kelly's Stables.
And Ralph wouldn't let him in.
Really? Max was that much younger, I didn't realize.
Yeah. He would stand outside and listen to us, you know.
Well, when you were at Minton's, didn't Max come up there?
Oh, yeah. Max -- he got the message. You know, I gave him the message after. Personally I gave Max the message.
Art? Well, he used to come to Minton's all the time.
Sometimes we'd let him sit in with us and all that. But Max was working with Bird at Clark Monroe's Uptown House.
So they would work like 5:00 o'clock in the morning, 6:00 o'clock in the morning.
And we'd finish at Minton's about 4:00.
So then we would all head for Monroe's Uptown House.
There we would sit in and discuss those different things, you know.
About drumming and this and that and the other thing.
But Max used to whistle when he played. Always whistle. I don't care what tune was playing, he would whistle. Not the tune, but whistle for himself.
Yeah. He would always whistle when he played.
